text_fidelity_a:
Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd Comes packed in a nice sturdy box. Inside the play yard is in a nice nylon bag.
Just pull the 2 velcro straps open, take off the wrap around/bottom part of play yard, pop the play yard open, insert bottom pad.
It wasn't until I was packing this back up that I found the instructions. They are in a small pocket that's on the wrap around/bottom pad part of play pen. With that said, we had a little trouble getting this set up but, finally got it figured out without instructions.
When opening, before you push the middle part of the bottom down, straighten and lock the side rails up. If you open it up all the way, the two smaller sides won't lock into place. Pull the red strap back up a bit then click them and push the bottom back down.

The bottom pad is a bit thin and it's a little shorter than the play yard is. Nothing that I would take a star away for.
Once set up, it seems sturdy enough to keep a small child safe.
There is nice padding around the entire top. Even the release buttons are under the padded top rail so there's no chance of child pinching any fingers.
Has nice plastic wheels on one side so you can easily lift one side and roll it to another location.
The top arching top attachment is cute with 2 small monsters attached to it. It just snaps onto the side rails and is nice and flexible. Not sure how much abuse that can withstand. And not sure what a bigger child would do to it if they were jumping in it.
Packing it back up was just a little difficult. Have to make sure the side rails are completely released so it closes up nicely to be packed. Nothing to complain about. Do it a few times and it will be a breeze.
The bottom pad wraps around the play yard. Put velcro straps through opening, pull tight, and push the velcro into place.
Slips back easily into nylon packing bag.
Nylon bag also has a couple handles for easy carrying and I can slip it onto a bike hook and hang it in the garage so it doesn't take up floor space.
This is a great play pen/play yard for a young child. Can toss it into the car and bring it anywhere you might need it.
I think the price is a great price for what you're getting.
I really don't have any complaints with this.
text_fidelity_b: Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd

Bright Starts Pop & Giggle Pond Pal Ball Popper Musical Toy, Ages 6 months + This frog is loud and a bit annoying, but it's still cute!

When this toy comes out of the box, you'll have to put together 3 different pieces. The head has to be attached to the body, and a little spring part attaches to the side. There are 6 different colored balls, too.

This toy does NOT come with batteries. You'll need 4 AA batteries, along with a small screwdriver(Phillips head or flat, either one) to get them into the toy.

There are 4 "piano" keys on the front that make sounds, and there's also the main button that will start the music playing and the mouth to bouncing. The inside of the mouth is soft. When the main button is pressed, the inside of the mouth will move around, and make the balls bounce. When the ball hits the center of the mouth, the bouncing will usually cause the ball to bounce outside of the mouth. This is fun for children to then go grabbing the stray balls. If the child is really young, you'll be the one grabbing the balls. (They will go rolling under couches and beds, so try to play it in an area that will result in minimal lost balls.)

Overall, this is a fun toy for young children/babies. The average mama of babies won't want it around too much, though. Between the noise and running after balls, it's a bit exhausting. For mamas of children that are old enough to chase after the balls, it's a great way to burn built up energy on a rainy day! (If playing on carpet, the balls most likely won't roll quite so much.)
text_fidelity_b: Bright Starts Pop & Giggle Pond Pal Ball Popper Musical Toy, Ages 6 months +

LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope OBI-Wan’s Hut 75270 Hot Toy Building Kit; Super Star Wars Starter Set for Young Kids (200 Pieces) Obi-Wan’s Hut is the first time Lego has ever done a set of Obi-Wan’s Hut! Kind of hard to believe, considering how many other iconic Star Wars scenes have been repeated over and over.

The hut is cool. I like how it folds into a cube and then opens for play. The inside is quite detailed, with lots of little details fans will like. There’s a carton of blue milk, a chest to hide Anakin’s lightsaber and the training droid, and the translucent blue hologram of Princess Leia.

I think the Princess Leia hologram will be a big draw for serious collectors, as there hasn’t been a piece like it before. The size of the hologram is just a tad bigger than a microfigure.

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll I have been around Barbie dolls my entire life. My mom collected them and my sister got into it. My daughter has had a few here and there, but none of them was the quality that this doll is. I did not expect it to be fantastic quality, but it even fell short of my lower expectations.

WHAT IS THE DOLL LIKE?
The doll comes in a clear plastic package which is not overly attractive, in fact it looks stark and not like the usual Barbie stuff. The doll itself is packaged with two pieces of plastic sticking out from inside her head. It is then attached to the board in the back so you have to cut those pieces to get it off of the backing. That means you have to be careful of the hair. Once you managed to do this, you have to stick the plastic ends back into the skull of the doll to keep the sharp ends from pricking your child or you.

The outfit is kind of cute and the colors are attractive. The doll itself is a rigid plastic doll- not the bendable twist and turn type that they have had in the past. The head piece has a knob type attachment which makes it able to move in almost any direction. The problem is in this case, the head is so easy to move it is borderline bobble head.

HOW DOES THE HAIR COLOR WORK?
The hair color looked like it would be a lot of fun! It has a plastic piece that is similar to a flat iron in shape. Inside the *flat iron* piece are a group of colored waxy blocks. The idea is that you comb the doll's hair and separate it into strands. You press the flat iron type piece over the hair, squeeze it shut as you draw the hair through and it leaves the color on the hair.

The hair is waxy in feel, probably to make the color work better than traditional Barbie hair. In this case, however, it does not seem to do much for the process. The hair colors are not too great. They come off as crumbly and waxy and very spotty on the hair. If you run your fingers over it, you will get some on your fingers. This will stain so if your child plays with this near anything white or light colored, it could stain it.

The color blocks are almost like you mix waxy crayons with silicone to make it a bit softer. The result is uneven kind of unimpressive color on the hair. It is not overly bright and does not look like the pictures promised.

THE BOTTOM LINE
My daughter was not impressed by this doll. The body is very rigid, making for a boring play toy. The hair is very uneven and has a waxy feel to it. The colors come out crumbly and uneven, and color blocks probably will only last for a day or two of constant play and then run out. The colors will stain some things so if you plan to let your child run free with this, you may regret it if you have anything white you don't want stained. The head is so easily moved that it is unpleasant to play with and use. The outfit is cute and colorful and the shoes are not too bad either.

My daughter kept saying that she expected more substantial color that was like a watercolor marker or something instead of a crumbly waxy substance that barely sticks to the hair in a few random spots. She kept taking out her other Barbie dolls and saying how much more she liked those. I give this two stars because it has a nice outfit, and if you want a disposable toy for your child, it will serve the purpose. If you want a sturdy toy they will play with over and over, I am thinking this might not be it for you.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll

ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls 3 stars

This stroller is very cute, and it is nice that it is in gender-neutral colors, so that boy children as well as girl children can enjoy this stroller. It can be used not just to hold baby dolls, but also stuffed animals.

This toy stroller resembles a typical human-baby, umbrella stroller in design and functionality. The difference between this and a real stroller, though, other than the miniature sizing, is that it is not sturdy. Therefore, there is a safety element in that your child may easily push or lean harder on its handles than it is built to withstand, and end up tripping and falling on top of or tumbling headfirst over it. If you have stairs in your house, this in particular could lead to a dangerous injury.

A major factor contributing to this flimsiness issue is the fact that the wheels are not at all strong and, overall, this toy is very cheaply made. It is certainly not constructed to stand up to the rather rugged treatment a toddler or preschooler would give to a toy like this.

In short, this doll stroller is certainly not a case of, "You get what you pay for." Because of the expensive price of this and all other Adora doll accessories, you'd think you'd be getting something really sturdy and long-lasting. Unfortunately, that is not the case with this stroller.
text_fidelity_b: ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls

text_fidelity_a:
PopSockets Fidget Train with Expanding PopSockets , Premium Fidget Toy, ASMR, Toys for Adults and Kids I am a terrible fidget and I am always on the lookout for toys and gizmos that will keep me focused so I can sit still and not distract everyone around me. I selected this thinking it would be similar to those blister-type pop toys. It's not, but it's still an effective toy for stress relief and focus. It's possibly a little too noisy for a meeting, though.

At a glance this thing looks like the sections might come apart. They do not. Instead, this is an accordion-style fidget toy that you pull and push on the ends to make it expand and contract. It can be bent, twisted slightly, partially expanded and completely expanded. The colors are soothing and the tactile feel is nice.

Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor [[VIDEOID:c9ed210fcea7bd15ff238268da66c6e5]] I really liked this classic game of Sorry. I hadn't played this game in over 25 years, so this is a fun blast from the past.

The game isn't as silly or as random as I remember it. For a random move your pawn game, there is actually a decent amount of strategy involved.

The rules were a bit confusing, since they used the old 1959 rules. Here's my summary of the rules: You can only move your pawns out of start if you pick a 1, 2, or sometimes a Sorry card. If you get a 1 or a 2, then you only move out to the first circle. You only slide when you get on the first part of the slide. If you can't move, you don't move, and you need an exact count to get into the Home square. Follow the rest of the instructions on the cards.

Pros:
+It's possible to win no matter how far behind a player is
+Great rendition of a classic game
+A lot of fun
+Great for any ages

Cons:
-The rules are a bit confusing. I had to clarify some of the rules on the internet.
-The game starts out very slowly
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version Kids like to do grown- up things and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera allows them to do just that. This is a fully- functioning camera specifically designed for the needs and desires of youngsters and it allows kids to take pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even upload them to a computer for further viewing and editing.

Many qualities make this camera one to consider and the first is the memory. This is sold as a child's camera, but it has a surprisingly high level of memory and is capable of holding up to 400 pictures! This is much better than I expected and with this much memory, it will take a long time before kids exceed the available space. They can walk around the house ansd snap picture after picture without worrying that the memory will fill.

Another positive aspect with the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is its durability. This camera is made from plastic with a rubberized edge that makes it easy to hold and highly resistant to breakage. My girls have dropped it several times and it continues to work regardless. It is also very entertaining. Not only can kids take their own pictures of mom, dad, the family dog, and their friends, but they can also add to the fun by using the editing feature. The silly editing allows kids a chance to take an ordinary picture and make it look funny.

So, the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is fun for kids, but are there any cons? Well, there are a few but they are minor enough to overlook. One is the viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is quite small and some images will be barely perceptible. It would be completely unacceptable to adults, but kids will likely find it perfectly fine. Then, one has to consider the picture quality. This camera has only 0.3 megapixels and that means the clarity of the pictures is well below average. Once again, kids are not likely to care. They will so enjoy having their own camera and taking their own pictures that they won't even notice or mind the fuzzy images.

Kids like to mimic adults and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is likely to be a hit with most youngsters for this and other reasons. As I said, the clarity of the photos isn't the best and the camera does have a few other minor flaws, but none of this will matter to most children. The ability to take their own pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even view them on a computer will be more than enough to please the young camerabug in your home.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version

There’s not a ton to build here, compared to other sets in this price point. There’s only 40 pieces in the set, many of which are small vet tools. The cube is the big draw.

My favorite part for this set, and actually for all the play cubes, is that the surprise is always the same animal. For example, Mia always comes with a rabbit. It’s the color of the animal that is the surprise. The colors are pink, purple, blue, or gold.

The box includes a mini poster that shows all the play cubes and the pets they come with. The poster also indicates there will be a Series 2 of the play cubes.

I wish that instead of using traditional stickers, Lego had gone with something like window clings or small decals, so that kids could more easily decorate and change the look of the cubes. Because the builds are somewhat bland, it’s really the stickers that add life to this set. I think it would be so much cooler if kids could swap the stickers.

But after about 10 minutes, the blue light starts to fade, then the green light starts to fade, until only the red light is working.  If turned off and left to sit and rest for a while, then all three light begin to light up and work again, but eventually again only the red light will remain lit.  This happened with all of the necklaces and bracelets in the box.  So as long as the lights are not needed to stay on for long periods of time, they are nice.  If needed for longer periods, two bracelets or necklaces or one of each could be used to alternate between them to give each one a rest by turning it off to refresh the colors.  So if handing these out for Halloween treats, I would recommend giving kids two in order to compensate for the lights not working all the time.

text_fidelity_a:
DWD INA Hatching Dragon GEN [[VIDEOID:86cf3e64e0b55c3de87641f5762af581]] I couldn't wait for Toothless to arrive! I've been collecting animatronic robotic toys since they were first introduced by Hasbro. I would have been over the moon of these were available when I was a kid and I adore him.

I've decided to post the video of Toothless hatching since you only get to enjoy that once and I preserved all the pieces, but you have to remove some internal part in order to place him back in his half shell where he sleeps,

I collect them so I saved everything. If you set him on a flat surface he rocks so it's best to keep him in his shell for extra stability and cuteness factor.😍

HATCHING::
The process takes about 20 minutes and you get to encourage him on his journey. He responds with adorable sounds to show you he is trying his hardest to meet you. His eyes flash and he makes grunting and light struggling sounds. 😍

A DRAGON IS BORN: 🐣
Toothless greets you with cooing with flapping wings, head tilts, and happy sounds.🐥

PLAYING:
He has 7 settings and play modes with 4 touch sensors and responds with different actions and sounds depending upon which sensor is activated by touch. Toothless is equipped with a mic and reacts to voice. Place his fish near his mouth and he makes eating sounds, but his mouth doesn't open or close. In blast mode, there are two blue LED lights on each side of his mouth that flash and he makes a photon blast power-up sound. He makes several sounds (I haven't counted them all yet) with affectionate noises to encourage interaction. ❤️

Overall Toothless is a MUST HAVE for anyone who enjoys robotic toys. I would have been over the moon💗🌙 if this were available when I was growing up and I don't know of any child who would not enjoy him. I certainly do. I would rate him at 4 1/2 stars due to the price. This is a well thought out and high-quality toy. I absolutely adore him 😍, but he lacks some of the more sophisticated programming and functionality of my other animatronic robotic pets. I still highly recommend him because he is cute and unique. If you saw the movie you'll love and enjoy him all the more.

** If you found this review to be helpful at all, please take a moment and click the button below to let Amazon know. Thank you 😊 **
text_fidelity_b: DWD INA Hatching Dragon GEN

Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition A nice update to an old game. I threw this in my shopping cart while out Christmas shopping. So I did not buy it on Amazon, but I am an Amazon Prime member. Cars 3 Monopoly Jr. is played just like regular Monopoly Jr. Only the pieces, property names, and chance cards have a Cars 3 theme. The rules are exactly the same. For those of you who do not know, Monopoly Jr. is a simplified version of Monopoly. You don't build houses or hotels. Mortgages on property is not a thing. The money is also way more simple. You still go to "jail." You will collect $2. However, there is literally no strategy involved. Just be the one to have the most money once one person goes bankrupt and you win. Monopoly Jr. does not end in arguments or tears (so long as your child can handle the issue of losing, which I will explain later.) Monopoly Jr. will not be the source of a deep rift through the family. You will find that you're still friends with people after the game is over. Game play is fast, you will not be playing into the wee hours of the morning trying to negotiate a loan because you landed on Park Place.

I like board games because it gets me and my son together and playing together. Screens are not involved. However, do understand that teaching 3-5 year olds how to play board games is a long process. At the end of the day, the point of playing games like this with kids this young is to get them using various skills. Skills such as paying attention, following multiple steps, counting, and taking turns. I would recommend holding off on competitive board games until after you have played a few cooperative board games. Such as [[ASIN:B006S9MUPU Peaceable Kingdom / Race to the Treasure! Cooperative Board Game]] or [[ASIN:B002V3RCE6 Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It]] Why? Because I found it helpful to play cooperative style games after playing competitive games ended in broken pieces and a broken spirit. Now at 5, it's still tough, but he's more capable of receiving the lesson that there are winners and there are losers. If your child gets really heartbroken when they lose, definitely get cooperative games before you get this one.

I would recommend this only for children starting at 5 years of age if you have spent time playing other board games, especially cooperative style board games.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition

But they were also interested in trying the interactive app. They downloaded it first but were a little disappointed that they needed to build the train before using it. The whole line seems a little childish, but it is obviously aimed at a younger audience that is addicted to screens and collecting.

Once built they tried the app and enjoyed it well enough. It seems to be a little like pokeman go in that you collect the ghosts. It has simple game play and some interesting interaction with the set. It is a little kitschy, and a little fun but not a lasting game. Definitely seems marketing driven.

But all in all, it is a fun set, it has some incredible pieces and while the set will probably be cannabalized quickly, it was enjoyed a lot during the build. Nice set.

Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray) For my daughter's sake, I would give this camera 5 stars. It is the longest lasting favorite toy any of my kids have ever received, EVER. I bought it for my then 7 year old daughter for Christmas 2 years ago, and it is still her very favorite toy at age 9. She plays with it almost daily, takes it with her on trips and to important events, and shows everyone the pictures she takes. I think not much more praise can be had for a toy than for it to be beloved after two full years of daily play! But I wills say, her expectations for it are different than mine. She doesn't care about printing the pictures out. She likes taking them and looking at them on the viewfinder, projecting them on the wall, and using the added features to make funny frames around the people and funny sounds. That's all she wants from it, and it delivers that perfectly.

BUT, as a parent, I would have hoped the screen would be better quality. When you look at it, it's sort of blurry and got lines through it. Frankly, sometimes it's hard to tell what I'm looking at. This doesn't bother my now 9 year old daughter AT ALL. But it is disappointing to me because I know the technology exists to make that better.

The quality of pictures is also not great when uploaded onto my computer (which I've only done a couple of times). It's VERY pixelated. Again, this isn't a feature my daughter cares about, so take that into account, but for me I wish that the option were there to print out a decent quality print because sometimes she takes really awesome shots that I wish I could save.

This camera is also super tough. Despite being dropped and thrown around and fought over by siblings for the last 2 years, it still works perfectly. The batteries last her generally a few months, depending on play. But they're just AA's, so no biggie to change them out.

Really, I am most impressed that this toy continues to make her so happy. I think Playskool could go a long way to making the picture/screen quality better, even for kids, but that's just a mom talking!
text_fidelity_b: Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray)

Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009) This is a really cool and interesting game! I wasn't sure what to expect based on the box and description, but unlike other contraption based games I've played (like the classic "mouse trap" from my youth), this is more of a cooperative play game.
There are 4 strings that move a (clearly mission-impossible inspired) suspended character around the playing board, and it takes careful pulling and releasing each of them as a group effort to navigate properly, sort of like a marionette puppet meets a corporate team building activity. There are some things to do like remove security cameras and traps but the truth is, the real fun doesn't start until you open up the jewel cage.
Once the cage is open, there's a countdown (you can hear the spring noise whirring as soon as it opens) and the police car starts to slowly circle the board. If you make it to the getaway car with the jewel before the car makes it to block your path, you win! If, however, you take too long, the police car will spring into place and block your path. Hilarity ensues as players start to panic and lose their cool, and in the end, whether you make it or not, it felt exciting.
Things I like about the game:
- It is cooperative, not individual. So you don't "beat" another player, you work as a team to complete the task in time.
- The mechanical game board is unique and really fun to learn
- It does NOT require batteries! The board uses spring loaded timers where necessary, no electricity. This is cool in a decidedly analog way.
- People can walk over and see how it is played and join with very little instruction

Things I did not, however, like:
- The truth is, when playing with my kids, we sort of skipped the first part of the game and just jumped to the jewel part. The designers of this game tried to make it longer by adding disarming traps and pulling security cameras in particular order based on cards, but it felt tedious after a few rounds. Really the fun part is the end. The whirring police car gives a sense of danger and urgency that makes it fun.
- That little spy is suspended by strings that get tangled so quickly and easily. It feels like I sneeze and they are tangled. Out of the box, I had to spend time untwisting it before we played for the first time, so be careful.

That being said, the game is TON of fun for different ages and we actually had some guests come over who looked at it and wanted to play too (adults AND kids). They all asked where to to get it, so it might become a regular thing found in our neighborhood. I'd say it deserves 5 stars, it's been a while since a game sparked this much interest that wasn't on a screen.
text_fidelity_b: Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009)

MEGA Corviknight Building Set With 340 Compatible Bricks and Pieces and Poké Ball, Toy Gift Set I’ve built a handful of the different Pokemon sets from Mega Construx. Pokemon aren’t always suited to block form, but I think the finished Corviknight looks good. It’s easily recognizable as Corviknight.

The feet and wings are built with ball-and-socket joints, so they are poseable. The Corviknight can stand on its own to be displayed, or posed into an attack position with the wings outstretched. The wing feathers are made from a flexible plastic that looks cool.

text_fidelity_a:
Simba Steffi Love - Hawaii Camper, Multicolor I am overall satisfied with my order of the Simba Steffi Love Camper Set. This arrived very well packaged for shipping. It was not overly difficult to remove from the box as most of the securing straps simply untied. There were several pieces of clear tape that needed to be removed. I do like that this set included a Steffi Love doll. It's an overall nice doll with articulated ankles and knees. I do wish that the elbows were also articulated, but they are not. She has shoes, a simple dress and sunglasses. She has underpants imprinted on her plastic pelvis. I do not advise to remove the elastic on her hair as the plugged hair will show the widely spaced hair plugs and be less than attractive.

The first impression of the playset inside the packaging is that it's very cute and attractive. The camper itself is not as durable as I had hoped. This will not stand up to rough play. I would not at all advise this to be accessible to toddlers or careless children because if one tried to use it as a seat or step-stool, it would break easily. The wheels are held in place with a metal rod, this would be a safety hazard if it came out of place. The many small accessories are also not appropriate for very small children as they could pose a choking hazard. There is not enough leg room in the two front seats for the doll's legs, they must be bent to the side or the doll has to sit sideways. Not all of the doors are well-molded to close completely. Some stickers are included, which is nice as one side of the camper already is decorated with stickers, leaving the opposite side blank. Several packets of accessories are included so the dolls can use props for various activities such as cooking, lounging and even showering. The small accessories are the best point of this playset.

I personally do not find this camper set to be a good value at it's current price point. There are too many issues that will lead to frustration in play. Primarily, the type of plastic material used to mold the camper is prone to failure as it's not at all durable. The play patterns of most small children will prove to be the source of frustration or failure of the toy. This type of plastic is prone to shattering and can produce sharp edges if broken. For many children, this will be a short-lived disposable toy. This would be most ideal for children that play gently and are able to keep small toys well organized and enjoy playing with fashion dolls. The camper itself measures about 22" long, 11" wide and 9 1/2" tall. This will need a significant amount of storage space, and would not easily withstand being stored stacked with other toys in a toybox. This would be best 'parked' under a bed, in a closet or on a shelf between play sessions to avoid a tripping hazard. I hope that my experience with this camper set is helpful as you kindly click the button below.
text_fidelity_b: Simba Steffi Love - Hawaii Camper, Multicolor

Hot Wheels Marvel Avengers Assemble Avengers 5-Pack [Amazon Exclusive] As superhero cars go, there really only is the Batmobile. That said, Hot Wheels has given in a go to design what they think are representative of the Avengers. Any purist will recognize many Avengers missing, depending who they consider the official team, like Black Widow, Ant Man, and others. All of these guys are members without question.

The cars look sharp. Like any Hot Wheels car, each is well-made. Below, I assess each vehicle, but note, it is tongue-in-cheek. These are toys. Iron Man and Thor can fly, and Hulk can jump pretty far. Those guys might have little use for cars.

Iron Man -- Red with silver. It should be red with some sort of yellow/gold.

Hulk -- Really? Does the Hulk have the finesse to drive?

Hawkeye -- His car reminds me of one the Munsters used to drive.

Thor -- Like the Iron Man car, it misses his overall color scheme. Needs more red. Old school body style, maybe 1974-ish.

Captain America -- Appropriately, red, white and blue.

Anthony Trendl
TreeFortBooks.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Marvel Avengers Assemble Avengers 5-Pack [Amazon Exclusive]

Fisher-Price Loving Family Beach Vacation Mobile Home The Fisher Price Loving Family Beach Vacation Mobile Home is a fun child's toy made for girls who love dolls and are always looking for new ways to play with them and enjoy them. This toy is a mobile home, but it is basically a child's dollhouse on wheels, folding open to reveal different rooms for hours of imaginative play.

My girls love their dolls and they own dozens of them, so they took an instant liking to this toy. Probably the most striking aspect of the toy is its colorful components. The interior features colors like green, pink, and blue and the accessories add some orange and other colors. The mobile home has some movable parts, too, like a microwave door that opens, an opening refrigerator door, turning steering wheel, and flipping toilet seat. The moving parts are few, but they still manage to stimulate the imagination. There are no included dolls with this toy, but most children will have no problem integrating the dolls they already have into the mobile home and enjoying the imagination that it inspires.

My kids like this toy and it is certainly an above average piece of fun, but if there is one way that Fisher Price could make it better, it would be to add some sounds, lights, or something else to stimulate the senses. Flashing lights would require batteries, which some may not like, but sound effects could be added without the need for batteries. The added sound of a honking horn, a motor starting up, flushing toilet, or something would make the toy more appealing to the average kid, most of whom still want something that appeals to the different senses.

Girls love dolls and the Fisher Price Loving Family Beach Vacation Mobile Home is a good toy for young girls who want a new way to display and play with their assortment of dolls. text_fidelity_a:
MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries Big & fast are the best ways to describe this RC racer!

At 1:10 scale, the unit ships with everything you need to run EXCEPT batteries for the RC transmitter. You will need to provide some AA batteries here. Also, make sure to charge your running batteries first.

Unfortunately, you will only get about 10-15 minutes of run time per charge. So having the 2 included battery packs is nice. Although, if you swap them out back-to-back, the one charging will not be ready to go before your second battery depletes. And charge time is roughly 4 hours EACH. So, you actually need A LOT of spare batteries if you want to run your car without any downtime.

Outside of this concern, the car is a lot like a hobby RC vehicle that you would assemble from scratch. But at a fraction of the cost. However, the parts are probably not hobby grade, but good enough for the intended audience of this vehicle.

In the mid-eighties, I was really into RC racing (A Tamiya Frog for those who remember), but even back then this was an expensive hobby (I was around 14, so everything was expensive!) as you always wanted to upgrade something - motor, servos, shocks, tires, etc... And I wasn't even running anywhere near top of the line stuff.

In contrast, this unit ships complete for right around $110.00. So, if you're just getting into the hobby (or re-entering), then this car will make a fun introduction/re-introduction without breaking the bank.

Lastly, this thing is FAST. It's rated right around 30-32MPH. That may seem slow when the only comparison you may have is driving in a car at that speed. However, seeing one of the RC cars rocket down the street at 30+ miles per hour will quickly alter your perspective!

Overall, this is a great out of the box setup that's a ton of fun for a kid, an adult or the kid in every adult!
text_fidelity_b: MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries

text_fidelity_a: BARWA 41 Pack Doll Clothes and Accessories 5 PCS Fashion Dresses 5 Tops 5 Pants Outfits 10 PCS Mini Dresses 10shoes 6 Necklace 5 Glasses for 11.5 inch Doll In fact, I just ordered another set. As an adult fashion doll collector and semi-professional photographer, I appreciate the fact that the clothes are from a variety of dolls. Some of the clothes are standard, wide hip Barbie size, while others are slimmer in the hips and torso (more like Model Muse) and still more fit dolls who are short and petite (like Barbie's sisters Skipper and Stacey). The Skipper and Stacey size tops look cute as midriff baring tops on a regular Barbie. I read a complaint below about the pants not fitting, but that's the way Mattel has been making pants since about 1999 when they introduced the first wide hip Barbie doll (the doll that we know today as a regular Barbie). The jeans are meant to fit below the waist and you have to tug to get them on and close them completely because they are meant to fit snugly. It's true, the clothing seams aren't always perfectly straight, but I have the same issue with Mattel Barbie clothes that I buy in person. Plus, the fabrics for these fashions are - for the most part - nicer than what Mattel has been offering lately. At the end of the day, when you consider that SINGLE ITEM Barbie brand clothing packs currently sell for $2.44 - $5.00 each, and Barbie brand complete fashion sets with shoes retail for $5.00 - $35.00 each, spending just under $2.00 for complete outfit is a great deal.

text_fidelity_a:
Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens I generally don't prefer electronic learning, but these are pretty cool. The Smart Letters each have three rubber feet that are spaced differently, and the tablet recognizes the letter when you gently place it on the tablet screen. It took about 10 minutes to download all 6 free apps (3 for letters, 3 for numbers) and to set up the quick profile. The apps are simple to use and well designed. Next is a summary of the 3 letter apps:

Bla Bla Box: spell out words and hear them read back to you
Alphamonster: choose a letter to hear the sound the letter makes and see a picture of a word beginning with that letter. See a picture of an item and identify what letter the item starts with. Hear a sound of a letter and identify the letter. See a cursive lowercase letter and identity the matching wooden uppercase letter. (In the settings you can pick which letters will appear throughout these challenges. The default is the entire alphabet but you can pick just a few if your child needs to focus on certain letters)
Vocabubble: game 1- pick any letter and as you repeatedly place the letter on the tablet, 8 different pictures of items beginning with that letter will fall down the screen. Game 2 - choose two letters, then pictures of items beginning with those two letters will fall down the screen and you tap the picture with the right letter in order for it to disappear. (This was a fun game my niece and nephew enjoyed playing together as they each held a letter. However, some pictures seemed too hard or random for a 5 year old, such as an Orca for the letter O... kids will think it's a Whale... or a Totem Pole or Quaill, etc)

My five year old niece and nephew enjoyed testing these for me and were definitely interested in the games. I'm excited to start my daughter with it when she turns three and I can see the number apps extending the usefulness of the product as she gets older. Four stars, not five, only because they do seem a bit pricey and also because the accent on the American English setting we tried out is a bit odd at times.
text_fidelity_b: Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens

text_fidelity_a:
Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure (Due to the malfunctions on our particular dog, and the fact that he doesn't walk at all, I was tempted to give it 3 stars, but he's so cute and fun, I went with 4.)

I have a few Paw Patrol fans in my house, so this is a pretty amazing toy.

By pressing the badge on the front of Chase, your children are given a mission. Chase talks and interacts through these missions. For example, chickens have gotten loose, and your child needs to help gather them up. The net compartment opens up, and your child will fire the net out. Chase comments on catching one, and then asks for the net to be reloaded. (One time the net got stuck, and didn't fire out, but he still exclaimed praise at catching a chicken, so it's not perfect.) He won't interact to various things that your child says, but he does have built in interaction, which is still pretty cool.

There are 24 different missions, and Chase moves around a bit through these. I was expecting him to walk a bit, but he never did. He just moves his head around, and moves from crouching to standing positions. There are two compartments on his backpack. One has a net launcher. The other has a microphone(that your child can talk into) and a flashlight. There are various buttons for each feature. (One for opening each compartment, one on the net launcher to launch, one to make the light come on the flashlight, and one to turn on the microphone.) Some of the items come on automatically through missions, but others require your child's assistance, when Chase asks.

Although this is an awesome toy that I'm pretty sure any Paw Patrol fan will love, we did have a couple of negatives with ours.

When the box was first opened, the head was detached a bit, but thankfully, it went back on pretty easily. Also, the button to launch the microphone/flashlight wouldn't work. I tried everything I could to make it work, short of tearing it apart, and tried numerous times, but it never worked. It didn't work when it was supposed to automatically open during missions, either. Thankfully, we can just pull that compartment open. During missions when a child is asked to launch the microphone/flashlight, pulling open the door makes the task recognized, just as if the button worked. So, it's not a huge deal, but still disappointing.

I really do wish he walked a bit, too! The way he's designed, it looked as if he would.

A couple of notes:
-This toy DOES come with batteries, but require 4 AA if you'd like to buy extras.
-If your child can read, know that the box this is delivered in says what's inside, though there are no pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure
